blocks.task_summary: Find the two values of b such that y = x^3 + 3x^2 + b has exactly two x-axis intercepts.
method_path: vary b and observe when a stationary point of the cubic lies on the x-axis
determine b = 0 (when P(0, b) touches x-axis) and b = −4 (when local minimum at x = −2 touches x-axis)

evidence.basis: M1 for varying b with a = 3 or evidence that b = 0 case is considered; A1 for b = −4, 0.

blocks.task_summary: Write the set of b values for which y = x^3 + 3x^2 + b has exactly one x-axis intercept.
method_path: deduce from part (a) that b < −4 or b > 0 gives exactly one x-intercept

evidence.basis: A1 for b < −4 or b > 0.

blocks.task_summary: Write the set of b values for which y = x^3 + 3x^2 + b has exactly three x-axis intercepts.
method_path: deduce from part (a) that −4 < b < 0 gives exactly three x-intercepts

evidence.basis: A1 for −4 < b < 0.

blocks.task_summary: Write the set of b values for which y = x^3 − 3x^2 + b has exactly two x-axis intercepts.
method_path: determine that when a = −3, stationary points at x = 0 (y = b) and x = 2 (y = b − 4) give exactly two intercepts for b = 0, 4

evidence.basis: A1 for b = 0, 4.

blocks.task_summary: Write the set of b values for which y = x^3 − 3x^2 + b has exactly one x-axis intercept.
method_path: deduce that b < 0 or b > 4 gives exactly one x-intercept

evidence.basis: A1 for b < 0 or b > 4.

blocks.task_summary: Write the set of b values for which y = x^3 − 3x^2 + b has exactly three x-axis intercepts.
method_path: deduce that 0 < b < 4 gives exactly three x-intercepts

evidence.basis: A1 for 0 < b < 4.

blocks.task_summary: For exactly three x-axis intercepts, state whether each point of zero gradient is above or below the x-axis.
method_path: state that the two stationary points lie on opposite sides of the x-axis

evidence.basis: A1 for 'one point of zero gradient is located on either side (of the x-axis)' or equivalent.

blocks.task_summary: Show that the curve has stationary points at P(0, b) and Q(−2a/3, 4a³/27 + b).
method_path: differentiate to obtain dy/dx = 3x² + 2ax
set dy/dx = 0 and factor to x(3x + 2a) = 0
solve to obtain x = 0 and x = −2a/3
verify P(0, b) is a stationary point and substitute x = −2a/3 into y = x³ + ax² + b
simplify to y = 4a³/27 + b to confirm Q(−2a/3, 4a³/27 + b)
accepted_alternatives: Substitute x = 0 and x = −2a/3 directly into dy/dx = 3x² + 2ax to verify each yields zero, then substitute x = −2a/3 into y = x³ + ax² + b and simplify to 4a³/27 + b (Method 2).

evidence.basis: Method 1: (A1) dy/dx = 3x² + 2ax; (M1) solve dy/dx = 0; (A1) x = 0, −2a/3; AG for P; (M1) substitute x into y; (A1) simplify to 4a³/27 + b. Method 2: (A1) dy/dx; (M1) substitute x=0 or x=−2a/3; AG for P; (A1) verify dy/dx=0 at both; (M1) substitute into y; (A1) simplify to y-coordinate.

blocks.task_summary: Find d²y/dx² and classify P and Q as local maximum or minimum when a > 0 and b > 0.
method_path: find d²y/dx² = 6x + 2a
evaluate at x = 0: d²y/dx² = 2a > 0 → P is a local minimum
evaluate at x = −2a/3: d²y/dx² = −2a < 0 → Q is a local maximum

evidence.basis: A1 for d²y/dx² = 6x + 2a; R1 for P is local minimum (2a > 0 when a > 0); R1 for Q is local maximum (−2a < 0 when a > 0).

blocks.task_summary: Determine whether P and Q are above or below the x-axis when a > 0 and b > 0.
method_path: note b > 0 and 4a³/27 + b > 0 when a > 0, b > 0, hence both P and Q lie above the x-axis

evidence.basis: A1 for both above the x-axis; accept a labelled sketch clearly showing this.

blocks.task_summary: For a < 0 and b > 0, state whether P is a local max or min and whether it is above or below the x-axis.
method_path: classify P as a local maximum (since a < 0 gives d²y/dx² = 2a < 0 at x = 0) and state it is above the x-axis (b > 0)

evidence.basis: A1 for P is a local maximum and is above the x-axis.

blocks.task_summary: State the conditions on a and b for Q to be below the x-axis.
method_path: state 4a³/27 + b < 0 or equivalently b < −4a³/27

evidence.basis: A1 for 4a³/27 + b < 0 or equivalent inequality, e.g. b < −4a³/27.

blocks.task_summary: Prove that if 4a³b + 27b² < 0 then y = x³ + ax² + b has exactly three x-axis intercepts.
method_path: factor 4a³b + 27b² < 0 as b(4a³ + 27b) < 0 or (b/27)(4a³ + 27b) < 0
deduce that b and (4a³/27 + b) have opposite signs
observe that b = y-coordinate of P and 4a³/27 + b = y-coordinate of Q
conclude P and Q lie on opposite sides of the x-axis
deduce that with stationary points on opposite sides the cubic must cross the x-axis exactly three times
accepted_alternatives: Split into two explicit cases: (1) b > 0 and 4a³/27 + b < 0 ⇒ a < 0 hence three intercepts; (2) b < 0 and 4a³/27 + b > 0 ⇒ a > 0 hence three intercepts (Method 2). The converse proof is also accepted for a maximum of 3 marks.

evidence.basis: Method 1: (M1) factor; (A1) b(4a³/27 + b) < 0 or (b)(4a³ + 27b) < 0; (A1) two sign cases; (R1) opposite signs ⇒ P and Q on opposite sides of x-axis; (R1) opposite sides ⇒ exactly three intercepts. Method 2: additional R1 for each subcase linking to sign of a.

blocks.task_summary: Write down an expression for the gradient of L in terms of x and y.
method_path: Express gradient m from y = mx as m = y/x

evidence.basis: y/x A1 [1 mark]

blocks.task_summary: Hence show that the gradient of C is given by dy/dx = -x/y.
method_path: Use perpendicular condition: gradient of C = -1/(gradient of L)
Substitute gradient of L = y/x to obtain dy/dx = -x/y

evidence.basis: dy/dx = -1/(y/x) = -x/y A1. Note: Award A1 for 'the gradient is the negative reciprocal of y/x' or m_C times y/x = -1.

blocks.task_summary: By solving the differential equation dy/dx = -x/y, show that the family of curves C has equation x^2 + y^2 = k where k is a parameter.
method_path: Separate variables: y dy = -x dx
Integrate both sides: y^2/2 = -x^2/2 + c
Rearrange to x^2 + y^2 = k where k = 2c

evidence.basis: attempts to separate variables x and y (M1). integral y dy = integral -x dx. y^2/2 = -x^2/2 + c A1. x^2 + y^2 = k AG [2 marks]

blocks.task_summary: On the same set of axes, sketch the curves y^2 = 16 - 8x and y^2 = 4 + 4x. Clearly label each curve and any x-intercepts. (Not required to find intersection points.)
method_path: Identify curves as sideways parabolas
Find x-intercept of y^2 = 16 - 8x: set y = 0 gives x = 2
Find x-intercept of y^2 = 4 + 4x: set y = 0 gives x = -1
Sketch two parabolic curves with correct shape, position, and two intersection points in QI and QIV

evidence.basis: two parabolic shaped curves with approximately correct shape/position (e.g. two intersection points, in first and fourth quadrant) A1A1. x-intercepts -1 and 2 A1 [3 marks]

blocks.task_summary: By solving y^2 = 4a^2 - 4ax and y^2 = 4b^2 + 4bx simultaneously, show that these curves intersect at the points M(a-b, 2sqrt(ab)) and N(a-b, -2sqrt(ab)).
method_path: Equate expressions: 4a^2 - 4ax = 4b^2 + 4bx
Simplify to a^2 - b^2 = x(a + b)
Factor LHS: (a - b)(a + b) = x(a + b)
Divide by (a + b) since a, b > 0 implies a + b > 0, giving x = a - b
Substitute x = a - b into either equation
Simplify to y^2 = 4ab, so y = +/- 2sqrt(ab)
accepted_alternatives: Alternative forms such as 4(a+b)(a-b) = 4(a+b)x or (a+b)(a-b) - x(a+b) = 0

evidence.basis: at intersection, 4a^2 - 4ax = 4b^2 + 4bx A1. attempts to factorize either LHS or RHS (M1). recognition that a + b > 0 R1. x = a - b A1. substitutes x = a - b into either equation and attempts to simplify (M1). y^2 = 4ab => y = +/- 2sqrt(ab) A1. AG [6 marks]

blocks.task_summary: At point M, show that the curves y^2 = 4a^2 - 4ax and y^2 = 4b^2 + 4bx intersect at right-angles.
method_path: Implicitly differentiate both curves: 2y(dy/dx) = -4a gives dy/dx = -2a/y, and 2y(dy/dx) = 4b gives dy/dx = 2b/y
Substitute y = 2sqrt(ab) at M
Obtain gradients: m_1 = -a/sqrt(ab) and m_2 = b/sqrt(ab)
Multiply gradients: m_1 times m_2 = -ab/(ab) = -1, confirming right-angle intersection
accepted_alternatives: Chain rule differentiation: dy/dx = -2a/sqrt(4a^2-4ax) and dy/dx = 2b/sqrt(4b^2+4bx), then substitute x = a - b

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: attempts implicit differentiation on either curve (M1). dy/dx = -4a/(2y) and dy/dx = 4b/(2y) A1. substitutes y = 2sqrt(ab) (M1). dy/dx = -a/sqrt(ab) and b/sqrt(ab) A1. product = -1 A1. METHOD 2: chain rule (M1), correct derivatives A1, substitute x = a-b (M1), gradients A1, product = -1 A1. [5 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Show that g(x,y) = (y - x)/(y + x).
method_path: Substitute f(x,y) = -x/y and tan(pi/4) = 1 into formula

blocks.task_summary: Hence, by solving the homogeneous differential equation dy/dx = (y - x)/(y + x), find a general equation that represents this family of curves, G. Give your answer in the form h(x, y) = d where d is a parameter.
method_path: Substitute y = vx, giving dy/dx = v + x dv/dx
Form DE: v + x dv/dx = (vx - x)/(vx + x) = (v - 1)/(v + 1)
Rearrange to x dv/dx = (v-1)/(v+1) - v = -(1+v^2)/(1+v)
Separate variables: (1+v)/(1+v^2) dv = -dx/x
Integrate: (1/2)ln(1+v^2) + arctan(v) = -ln|x| + d
Substitute back v = y/x
Obtain (1/2)ln(1+(y/x)^2) + arctan(y/x) + ln|x| = d

evidence.basis: let y = vx (M1). dy/dx = v + x dv/dx (A1). v + x dv/dx = (v-1)/(v+1) (A1). attempts to express x dv/dx as single fraction in v (M1). x dv/dx = -(1+v^2)/(1+v) (A1). attempts to separate variables (M1). integral (1+v)/(1+v^2) dv = -integral 1/x dx. (1/2)ln(1+v^2) + arctan(v) = -ln x + d A1A1. (1/2)ln(1+(y/x)^2) + arctan(y/x) + ln x = d A1. [9 marks]

blocks.task_summary: By considering lim as alpha -> pi/2 of tan(alpha), show that, for all finite f(x,y), lim as alpha -> pi/2 of g(x,y) = -1/f(x,y).
method_path: Rearrange formula to g = (1/tan(alpha) + f)/(1/tan(alpha) - f) or use sin/cos
As alpha -> pi/2, tan(alpha) -> infinity so 1/tan(alpha) -> 0
Conclude g -> -1/f
accepted_alternatives: Using sin(alpha)/cos(alpha) substitution: g = (f cos(alpha) + sin(alpha))/(cos(alpha) - f sin(alpha)), then as alpha -> pi/2, cos(alpha) -> 0, sin(alpha) -> 1, so g -> 1/(-f) = -1/f

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: g = (1/tan(alpha) + f)/(1/tan(alpha) - f) M1. As alpha -> pi/2, 1/tan(alpha) -> 0, hence g -> -1/f R1 (dependent on M1). METHOD 2: uses sin/cos to form g = (f cos(alpha) + sin(alpha))/(cos(alpha) - f sin(alpha)) M1. As alpha -> pi/2, cos(alpha) -> 0, sin(alpha) -> 1, so g -> -1/f R1. [2 marks]
